title: Oncall Tacit Knowledge Transfer — Week of 2029-03-29
content:
Week overview:

This is a working log for the SRE oncall handoffs and tacit-knowledge transfer from the week of 2029-03-29. Goal: capture the practical operational learnings that are not in runbooks yet, prioritize follow-ups, and make the next shift smoother. Notes are intentionally informal — bits-to-capture and action items for the team.

Summary of key events:
- 2029-03-27 03:12 UTC — INC-2987: Intermittent 500s on hosted text-gen tier for region us-west-2. Root cause (preliminary): a combination of a memory leak in the batching worker (service: inference-batcher-v2) + degraded ephemerally-high GC churn on one node pool. Impact: 3.4% error rate spike for 18 minutes, latency p95 increased ~420ms above baseline.
- 2029-03-28 18:50 UTC — Near-miss: Autoscale lag caused queueing on dedicated clusters during a customer flood. No customer-facing errors (fallback worked), but observed token backlog growth ~2.2x for 12 minutes. Noted that autoscale policy threshold didn't account for sudden short-lived spikes from synchronous bursts.

SLO snapshot (rolling 28d):
- API availability (hosted text-gen): 99.94% (target 99.95%) — within margin but trending down due to recent noise.
- Median latency: 78ms (target 70ms) — small regression on batch-heavy hours.
- Error budget remaining: ~1.3% for the month.

Oncall handoff and tacit notes (what I told next shift):
- If you see a p95 bump without error rate rise, first check kv-cache saturation and batcher queues (kubectl top/pod logs for inference-batcher). Recent leak appears after ~48–72h of continuous warm-up; a restart of the offending pod clears it.
- For INC-2987, do NOT restart all batchers at once — restart one replica, validate metrics for 2 min, then proceed. Full-bounce causes transient latency spikes we observed previously.
- Autoscale notes: the dedicated autoscaler uses a 30s aggregation window followed by a 90s stabilization. For short bursts, trigger manual scale-up via the ops script (ops/scale_manual.sh) if queue growth exceeds 1.8x for >3 mins. Documented in slack thread #infra-autoscale (link in artifacts).

Immediate actions and owners:
- Rohan: follow up on memory leak stack traces; file a targeted bug in GH-PR-4215 with heap dumps and curated repro. (Due: 2029-04-03)
- Maya: tighten alerting rule for p95-latency (add secondary threshold at +150ms for 5m) and create a low-noise escalation path. (Due: 2029-04-02)
- Ethan: add a canary restart playbook to runbook (steps, checks, dashboards to watch). Post to Confluence and link to oncall deck. (Due: 2029-04-05)
- Sofia: revisit autoscaler policy and propose a short-burst mode (window adjustments + burst headroom). Draft proposal to eng-sre by 2029-04-06.

Runbook gaps discovered (notes-to-self):
- No documented procedure for extracting and sharing partial heap dumps from running batcher pods without killing them. Need a safe collection method (containers use shared tmpfs).
- The current incident checklist doesn't call out the queue-growth/backpressure metric (inference.queue_length), which is a better early signal than error-rate for batcher issues.
- Missing puppeteer steps for manually forcing KV cache invalidation for a noisy tenant.

Customer/CS escalations:
- One customer reported degraded responses during INC-2987. CS ticket created (CS-7124). Handed to customer-success with the incident summary and expected RCA timeline. Keep CS updated after Rohan's bug triage.

Low-friction mitigations already applied:
- Hotfix: rolled partial pod restart of inference-batcher in us-west-2 at 2029-03-27 04:01 UTC. Reduced the error spike immediately.
- Temporarily added a conservative rate-limit on long-running sync jobs for one enterprise tenant to avoid tail-chaining effects into the shared batcher. Contacted Solutions Eng to discuss longer-term QoS isolation.

Notes for improved observability:
- Add a derived metric: batcher_effective_mem_per_request = pod_memory_used / requests_in_last_5m. This helped us confirm memory trend faster in post-incident testing.
- Dashboards: create a combined view showing inference.queue_length, batcher_pod_mem_rss, request_latency_p95, and GC_pause_seconds. Put this on the 'oncall' dashboard as a 4-up panel.

Unresolved questions / discussion items for weekly sync:
- Is a per-tenant soft-QoS isolation (weight-limit in batching) worth the added complexity? (tradeoff: cost vs reliability)
- Should we reduce the autoscaler stabilization to 60s for dedicated clusters that have proven horizontal capacity? (ops vs noise)

Retrospective takeaway (short):
- The incident was combination-failure: subtle mem growth that only becomes visible under steady warm traffic + autoscaler thresholds tuned for average, not short spikes. Operational rule: prefer targeted restarts over full-service bounces unless we confirm broad corruption.

Appendix: quick commands and logs I used (copy for handoff)
- Check queue lengths: k get hpa,pod -l app=inference-batcher -o wide; kubectl exec -it batcher-0 -- curl localhost:9100/metrics | grep inference_queue_length
- Collect lightweight heap summary: kubectl exec batcher-0 -- pmap -x 1 | head -n 50  (note: needs procps in image)
- Tail candidate logs: kubectl logs -l app=inference-batcher -c worker --since=30m | grep -E "ERROR|OOM|GC"

End notes: leave feedback inline on this doc (especially if you took action during night shift). I want these tacit tips converted to concrete runbook steps over the next two weeks.

-- Ava
